The test image shows a tomato stem at a lateral branch junction with:
- Bleached, light tan/whitish stem tissue that appears water-soaked
- White cottony/fluffy material visible on the stem surface
- The lateral stem appears girdled and collapsing
- Dead/wilted tissue hanging to the right
- Lesion is on the stem (not at soil line)

This strongly suggests a stem disease with white mycelium. Key candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cotton-like mycelium, bleached stem) or **Southern_Blight** (also white mycelium but typically at soil line).

Now I'll use my 1 reference image view on Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot since the lesion is mid-stem (not soil line) and the bleached cottony appearance matches the description well.

The reference image confirms Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot shows bleached/whitened stem tissue with white mycelium girdling the stem, matching the test image well.

**Comparison:**
- Test image: Bleached tan/white stem at lateral branch junction, white cottony material visible, wilted/dead tissue hanging from the infected junction
- Reference: Bleached white stem with white mycelium, girdling at stem base with sclerotia visible

Both show the characteristic bleached, white-covered girdled stem. The test image lesion is at a lateral branch junction (higher on plant) rather than soil line, but Sclerotinia can infect at any stem point. The white cottony mycelium and bleached appearance are diagnostic for Sclerotinia Timber Rot.
